Watch Toronto indie-rock band Kiwi Jr. play the title track to their 2026 album, "Blowin' Up"
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Toronto band Kiwi Jr. released their latest album, "Blowin’ Up," in August 2026. The band’s fourth album since 2019, it is their first release on the Olympia, Washington-based label K Records. “It's cool to be on K now,” Kiwi Jr. frontman Jeremy Gaudet says. “[It was] always on our mind as an inspirational label and home to a lot of great artists.”

Kiwi Jr. visited The Current studio to play a couple songs from the new album and more, including the title track, above. 

Watch Kiwi Jr.'s full session here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KEWGhBAk_P0

Watch a studio session with Toronto indie-rock band Kiwi Jr.
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Toronto band Kiwi Jr. embraced a couple inspirations on their latest album, Blowin’ Up. Released in August 2026, Blowin’ Up — the band’s fourth album since 2019 — marks Kiwi Jr.’s first release on the Olympia, Washington-based label K Records. “It's cool to be on K now,” Kiwi Jr. frontman Jeremy Gaudet says. “[It was] always on our mind as an inspirational label and home to a lot of great artists.”

Secondly, the Torontonians had long been inspired by the music coming out of nearby Detroit, and they opted to record Blowin’ Up there. “The Detroit music stuff was on our mind constantly” during recording, Gaudet says. “We didn't think we were just going to show up for a week and make, like, a classic Detroit record or anything like that. But we were thinking of Iggy Pop and MC5 and the White Stripes and bands like that.”

author: The Current
description:
Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis talk about producing The Human League's album "Crash" and the single, "Human"
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

"Part of being a producer is problem solving," Jimmy Jam says. When working with The Human League on their 1986 album, "Crash," members of the Human League objected to a studio vocalist, Lisa Keith, singing on the track, "Human." The way Terry Lewis solved the problem was to write a spoken-word bridge. Not only did it solve the adversity within the studio, the lyrical addition changed the mood of the song and delivered what Jam says felt like "a gut punch."

The result was an amazing single, "Human," that went to No. 1, and The Human League continue to perform the song live to this day.

Hear more from Jimmy Jam in his and Terry Lewis’ interview with The Current’s Jill Riley in the video above. 

You can find Jam and Lewis’ complete interview here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bMhV5nKNH2E

title: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis on working with The Human League on the track, "Human"
